source: NCERT Class VI, Exploring Society: India and Beyond, Economics Ch. 2.

sections.heading: 1. Economic Activities
points: **Economic activities** = activities that involve **producing, exchanging or consuming goods and services**, usually to **earn income**.
**Non-economic activities** are done out of love, duty or leisure, without aiming to earn (e.g. helping a friend, playing).
Economic activities meet human **needs and wants**.

sections.heading: 2. Goods and Services
points: **Goods** = physical, tangible things that can be touched and stored (e.g. rice, cloth, a phone).
**Services** = useful activities done for others; they are **intangible** and cannot be stored (e.g. teaching, a bus ride, a haircut).
Both satisfy human wants.

sections.heading: 3. The Three Sectors of the Economy

sub: Agriculture, animal husbandry, fishing, forestry, mining.

points.text: **Secondary sector** — **manufacturing/industry**: turns raw materials into finished goods:
sub: e.g. making cloth from cotton, steel from iron ore, food products in factories.

points.text: **Tertiary (service) sector** — provides **services** that support the other two:
sub: e.g. transport, banking, trade, teaching, health, tourism, IT.

points: As an economy develops, more people move from the **primary** to the **secondary** and **tertiary** sectors.

sections.heading: 4. Producers, Consumers and Exchange
points: **Producers** make goods/provide services; **consumers** use them.
Goods and services are exchanged in **markets**.
Early exchange was by **barter** (goods for goods), which was difficult; **money** made exchange easy by acting as a common medium.
Money also serves as a **measure of value** and a **store of value**.

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Economic activity = producing/exchanging/consuming goods & services to earn income.
Goods = tangible (storable); services = intangible (cannot be stored).
Primary = from nature (farming, fishing, mining); Secondary = manufacturing; Tertiary = services.
Producers make; consumers use; exchange happens in markets.
Barter (goods↔goods) → money (common medium of exchange).

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **Mining and fishing are PRIMARY** sector (from nature), not secondary.
**Manufacturing** = secondary; **services** (transport, banking, teaching) = tertiary — don't swap.
**Goods** are tangible; **services** are intangible and cannot be stored.
Money's key advantage over barter = it is a **common medium of exchange** (no need for a double coincidence of wants).
